handbookNote: Idaho Code Title 51, Chapter 1, "Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts (2018)" (RULONA) -- Sections 51-101 through 51-133 (34 in-force sections; 51-119 is reserved), fetched directly from legislature.idaho.gov 2026-08-16. CLASSIFICATION: Idaho is an APPLICATION-ONLY notary commissioning state -- Sec. 51-121 lists the complete, exhaustive qualification set (age 18+, U.S. citizen/permanent legal resident, Idaho resident or place of employment/practice, able to read and write, plus a $10,000 surety bond or equivalent) and contains NO exam or training-completion requirement. NUANCE (why this matters and is preserved here): Sec. 51-122, titled "Course of Study," is a REAL statutory mandate -- "The secretary of state or an entity approved by the secretary of state shall offer regularly a course of study to applicants... The course must cover the laws, rules, procedures and ethics relevant to notarial acts." But the obligation runs to the STATE (shall offer), not the applicant (no "shall complete"/"shall pass" language anywhere, and Sec. 51-121's qualification list and Sec. 51-123's denial-grounds list never cross-reference Sec. 51-122). So this is a statutorily-mandated OFFERING, not a REQUIREMENT -- good marketing texture ("Idaho itself requires the state to make this material available") that does not reclassify the product as exam-prep. SECOND NUANCE: Sec. 51-121(3)(a)(ii) lets a state-employee applicant substitute the standard commercial $10,000 surety bond with an assurance from "the risk management office in the department of administration for the state of Idaho" when the commission is required for the scope of state employment -- an unusual self-insurance carve-out captured in the commissioning question bucket. CONTENT DEPTH: full RULONA text was fetched section-by-section (in-state/other-state/tribal/federal/foreign notarial-act recognition, remote/RON notarization under 51-114A, certificates and statutory short forms, compound acknowledgments, official stamp/stamping device specs, commissioning and bonding, discipline grounds, prohibited acts including the notario publico and unauthorized-practice-of-law restrictions, the notary database, fees, and misc. uniform-act/E-SIGN/savings provisions) -- more than sufficient to ground a genuine, non-padded question bank; no filler or invented facts were used to reach the question count. PRICING: $0.75 (75 cents) -- re-tiered 2026-08-16 against the AL/FL/GA/TX reference range (those 4 education-only tracks landed at 138-224 questions after depth expansion); Idaho's real content ceiling (148 questions) sits below that range, so it takes the middle 'solid but lighter' tier rather than the top $0.99 tier (reserved for states whose real content lands within/close to 138-224, e.g. DE/NH/ND/VA/WA/WV) or the bottom $0.50 tier (reserved for genuinely thin states like MN). Deliberately priced below the $9.99 tier reserved for states with a real mandatory exam, since this is self-study reference content on real Idaho notarial law, not exam prep.
